rules.quote: When an unsupported instruction is encountered and the PCPI feature is activated (see ENABLE_PCPI above), then pcpi_valid is asserted, the instruction word itself is output on pcpi_insn, the rs1 and rs2 fields are decoded and the values in those registers are output on pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2.
rules.condition: an unsupported instruction is encountered and PCPI is activated (ENABLE_PCPI)
rules.statement: The core asserts pcpi_valid, outputs the instruction word on pcpi_insn, and outputs the rs1 and rs2 register values on pcpi_rs1 and pcpi_rs2.

review.reason: Quote states the core asserts pcpi_valid and drives pcpi_insn, pcpi_rs1, pcpi_rs2 on an unsupported instruction with PCPI enabled. Observable at the interface.

rules.quote: An external PCPI core can then decode the instruction, execute it, and assert pcpi_ready when execution of the instruction is finished.
rules.condition: pcpi_valid asserted with an instruction
rules.statement: An external PCPI core can decode and execute the instruction and assert pcpi_ready when execution is finished.

review.reason: Quote says an external core can decode, execute and assert pcpi_ready. It is optional behaviour of the slave, exercised by a scenario.

rules.quote: Optionally a result value can be written to pcpi_rd and pcpi_wr asserted.
rules.condition: instruction execution finished
rules.statement: The PCPI core can optionally write a result value to pcpi_rd and assert pcpi_wr.

review.reason: Quote says a result can optionally be written to pcpi_rd with pcpi_wr asserted. Optional slave behaviour, exercised by a scenario.

rules.quote: The PicoRV32 core will then decode the rd field of the instruction and write the value from pcpi_rd to the respective register.
rules.condition: PCPI core returns a result with pcpi_wr asserted
rules.statement: The PicoRV32 core decodes the rd field of the instruction and writes the pcpi_rd value to the respective register.

review.reason: Quote states the core decodes rd and writes pcpi_rd to that register. This needs register-file visibility, so a scenario is the right check.

rules.quote: When no external PCPI core acknowledges the instruction within 16 clock cycles, then an illegal instruction exception is raised and the respective interrupt handler is called.
rules.condition: no external PCPI core acknowledges the instruction within 16 clock cycles
rules.statement: An illegal instruction exception is raised and the respective interrupt handler is called.

review.reason: Quote states an illegal instruction exception is raised and the handler is called when no PCPI core acknowledges within 16 cycles. Tested with a scenario.

rules.quote: A PCPI core that needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction, should assert pcpi_wait as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts pcpi_ready.
rules.condition: the PCPI core needs more than a couple of cycles to execute an instruction
rules.statement: The PCPI core should assert pcpi_wait as soon as the instruction is decoded successfully and keep it asserted until it asserts pcpi_ready.

review.reason: Quote says a slow PCPI core should assert pcpi_wait once decoded and keep it asserted until pcpi_ready. 'More than a couple of cycles' is vague, but the pcpi_wait/pcpi_ready relation is checkable from interface signals.

rules.quote: This will prevent the PicoRV32 core from raising an illegal instruction exception.
rules.condition: pcpi_wait is asserted by the PCPI core
rules.statement: Asserting pcpi_wait prevents the PicoRV32 core from raising an illegal instruction exception.

review.reason: Quote states that pcpi_wait prevents the core from raising an illegal instruction exception. Tested by a scenario.

rules.quote: mul performs an XLEN-bit×XLEN-bit multiplication of rs1 by rs2 and places the lower XLEN bits in the destination register. mulh, mulhu, and mulhsu perform the same multiplication but return the upper XLEN bits of the full 2×XLEN-bit product, for signed×signed, unsigned×unsigned, and rs1×unsigned rs2 multiplication.
rules.condition: executing mul
rules.statement: mul multiplies rs1 by rs2 as XLEN-bit values and writes the lower XLEN bits of the product to the destination register.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: mul performs an XLEN-bit×XLEN-bit multiplication of rs1 by rs2 and places the lower XLEN bits in the destination register. mulh, mulhu, and mulhsu perform the same multiplication but return the upper XLEN bits of the full 2×XLEN-bit product, for signed×signed, unsigned×unsigned, and rs1×unsigned rs2 multiplication.
rules.condition: executing mulh, mulhu or mulhsu
rules.statement: mulh, mulhu and mulhsu return the upper XLEN bits of the 2×XLEN-bit product for signed×signed, unsigned×unsigned and signed rs1×unsigned rs2 respectively.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: If both the high and low bits of the same product are required, the recommended code sequence is mulh rdh,rs1,rs2 followed by mul rdl,rs1,rs2. mulhu or mulhsu can be used instead of mulh if appropriate.
rules.condition: both high and low bits of the same product are required
rules.statement: Use mulh (or mulhu/mulhsu if appropriate) rdh,rs1,rs2 followed by mul rdl,rs1,rs2 to obtain both halves.

review.reason: A recommended code sequence, so SHOULD fits. Nothing to check in hardware.

rules.quote: Note that the source register specifiers, rs1 and rs2, must be in same order and rdh cannot be the same as rs1 or rs2.
rules.condition: using the recommended mulh/mul fusion sequence
rules.statement: Source specifiers rs1 and rs2 must be in the same order in both instructions, and rdh must not be the same as rs1 or rs2.

review.reason: The quote says 'must' for the software sequence. It is a constraint on the programmer.

rules.quote: Microarchitectures can then fuse these into a single multiply operation instead of performing two separate multiplies.
rules.condition: mulh followed by mul of the same operands
rules.statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single multiply operation instead of two separate multiplies.

review.reason: Fusion is optional ('can'), so MAY fits.

rules.quote: mulw is an RV64 instruction that multiplies the lower 32 bits of the source registers, placing the sign extension of the lower 32 bits of the result into the destination register.
rules.condition: RV64 mulw
rules.statement: mulw multiplies the lower 32 bits of the source registers and writes the sign extension of the lower 32 bits of the result to the destination register.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: Note: In RV64, mul can be used to obtain the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit product, but signed arguments must be proper 32-bit signed values, whereas unsigned arguments must have their upper 32 bits clear.
rules.condition: RV64 mul used to obtain the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit product
rules.statement: Signed arguments must be proper 32-bit signed values and unsigned arguments must have their upper 32 bits clear.

review.reason: A usage constraint on operands, stated by the quote. Not checkable from interface signals.

rules.quote: div and divu perform an XLEN bits by XLEN bits signed and unsigned integer division of rs1 by rs2, rounding towards zero. rem and remu provide the remainder of the corresponding division operation.
rules.condition: executing div, divu, rem or remu
rules.statement: div and divu perform XLEN-bit signed and unsigned division of rs1 by rs2 rounding towards zero; rem and remu return the remainder of the corresponding division.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: For rem, the sign of a nonzero result equals the sign of the dividend.
rules.condition: rem with a nonzero result
rules.statement: The sign of a nonzero rem result equals the sign of the dividend.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: If both the quotient and remainder are required from the same division, the recommended code sequence is div rdq,rs1,rs2 followed by rem[rdr,rs1,rs2]. divu and remu can also be used if appropriate.
rules.condition: both quotient and remainder are required from the same division
rules.statement: Use div rdq,rs1,rs2 followed by rem rdr,rs1,rs2 (or divu and remu if appropriate).

review.reason: A recommended code sequence, so SHOULD fits.

rules.quote: Note that rdq can not be the same as rs1 or rs2.
rules.condition: using the recommended div/rem sequence
rules.statement: rdq must not be the same register as rs1 or rs2.

review.reason: 'Can not be the same' is a prohibition, so MUST_NOT fits.

rules.quote: Microarchitectures can then fuse these into a single divide operation instead of performing two separate divides.
rules.condition: div followed by rem of the same operands
rules.statement: Microarchitectures may fuse the two instructions into a single divide operation instead of two separate divides.

review.reason: Fusion is optional, so MAY fits.

rules.quote: divw and divuw are RV64 instructions that divide the lower 32 bits of rs1 by the lower 32 bits of rs2, treating them as signed and unsigned integers, placing the 32-bit quotient in rd, sign-extended to 64 bits. remw and remuw are RV64 instructions that provide the corresponding signed and unsigned remainder operations.
rules.condition: RV64 divw, divuw, remw, remuw
rules.statement: divw and divuw divide the lower 32 bits of rs1 by those of rs2 as signed and unsigned and write the 32-bit quotient sign-extended to 64 bits in rd; remw and remuw give the corresponding remainders.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: Both remw and remuw always sign-extend the 32-bit result to 64 bits, including on a divide by zero.
rules.condition: remw or remuw, including divide by zero
rules.statement: remw and remuw always sign-extend the 32-bit result to 64 bits, including on a divide by zero.

review.reason: Stated directly by the quote.

rules.quote: The quotient of division by zero has all bits set, and the remainder of division by zero equals the dividend. L is the width of the operation in bits: XLEN for div, divu, rem, and remu, or 32 for divw, divuw, remw, and remuw. Condition: Division by zero; Dividend: _x_; Divisor: 0; divu/divuw: 2^(L)-1; remu/remuw: _x_; div/divw: −1; rem/remw: _x_
rules.condition: division by zero
rules.statement: Division by zero returns all bits set (-1 for div/divw, 2^L-1 for divu/divuw) as quotient, and the remainder equals the dividend for rem/remw/remu/remuw.

review.reason: The quote gives the division-by-zero table.

rules.quote: Signed division overflow occurs only when the most-negative integer is divided by −1. The quotient of a signed division with overflow is equal to the dividend, and the remainder is zero. Condition: Overflow (signed only); Dividend: -2^(L-1); Divisor: −1; divu/divuw: --; remu/remuw: --; div/divw: -2^(L-1); rem/remw: 0
rules.condition: signed division overflow: most-negative integer divided by -1
rules.statement: On signed overflow the quotient equals the dividend (-2^(L-1)) and the remainder is zero.

review.reason: The quote gives the overflow table. The quotient equals the dividend and the remainder is 0.

rejected.quote: The optional Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI) can be used to implement non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor. The Pico Co-Processor Interface (PCPI) can be used to implement non-branching instructions in external cores:
rejected.condition: implementing non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor
rejected.statement: The PCPI can be used to implement non-branching instructions in an external coprocessor core.

review.reason: Descriptive overview of PCPI purpose; nothing to verify or exercise.

rejected.statement: Unsigned division overflow does not occur.

review.reason: A statement of fact ('cannot occur'). It gives no behaviour to verify or exercise.

rejected.quote: Further, where language standards mandate that a divide-by-zero exception must cause an immediate control flow change, only a single branch instruction needs to be added to each divide operation, and this branch instruction can be inserted after the divide and should normally be very predictably not taken, adding little runtime overhead.
rejected.condition: language standard mandates divide-by-zero exception causing immediate control flow change
rejected.statement: A single branch instruction may be inserted after each divide to implement the required control flow change.

review.reason: It describes software overhead for language-mandated divide-by-zero handling. No hardware behaviour to verify or exercise.

rejected.quote: Opcodes marked as _reserved_ should be avoided for custom instruction-set extensions as they might be used by future standard extensions.
rejected.statement: Opcodes marked as reserved should be avoided for custom instruction-set extensions, as future standard extensions might use them.

review.reason: This is design guidance for custom-extension authors, not DUT behavior. It cannot be checked by an assertion or exercised in a scenario, so there is nothing to verify.

rejected.quote: Major opcodes marked as _custom-0_ through _custom-3_ will be avoided by future standard extensions and are recommended for use by custom instruction-set extensions within the base 32-bit instruction format.
rejected.condition: When adding custom instruction-set extensions within the base 32-bit instruction format
rejected.statement: Major opcodes custom-0 through custom-3 are recommended for custom instruction-set extensions; future standard extensions will avoid them.

review.reason: This is a recommendation to ISA extension designers, plus a statement about future standard extensions. It describes no DUT behavior to verify or exercise.

questions.question: Is the 16-cycle timeout counted from pcpi_valid assertion? Does asserting pcpi_wait suspend the timeout indefinitely, or only until pcpi_ready? What happens if pcpi_wait is asserted after cycle 16?
questions.note: Not settled. The documents say the exception is raised when no PCPI core acknowledges within 16 clock cycles, and that pcpi_wait, kept asserted until pcpi_ready, prevents the illegal instruction exception. They do not say which event starts the 16-cycle count (pcpi_valid assertion is not stated), whether pcpi_wait suspends the timeout indefinitely, or what happens if pcpi_wait is first asserted after cycle 16.

questions.question: What does 'more than a couple of cycles' mean in cycles? When must pcpi_wait be asserted so that it counts as being asserted 'as soon as' the instruction is decoded?
questions.note: Not settled. 'More than a couple of cycles' is not quantified, and 'as soon as the instruction has been decoded successfully' has no cycle bound. The only hard limit given is the 16-cycle acknowledgement window. The designer must define the thresholds.

questions.question: Must pcpi_wr be asserted in the same cycle as pcpi_ready, or can it be asserted earlier? Is pcpi_rd sampled only when pcpi_ready is high?
questions.note: Not settled. The documents say pcpi_ready is asserted when execution finishes and that optionally a result is written to pcpi_rd with pcpi_wr asserted. They do not give the timing of pcpi_wr relative to pcpi_ready, and do not say whether pcpi_rd is sampled only when pcpi_ready is high. The designer must specify this.

questions.question: The quote for T1.1-04 says rdh cannot equal rs1 or rs2, but the mulh/mul pair is only safe if the first instruction does not overwrite a source of the second. T1.2-04 gives the same constraint for rdq. Should the testbench treat these as software-only constraints, or must it check hardware behaviour when they are violated?
questions.note: Not settled. The RISC-V text gives the rdh/rdq register restrictions as part of the recommended code sequence, so that microarchitectures can fuse the pair. It does not say what hardware must do when they are violated, and it does not say whether a testbench should check that case. The designer must decide whether these are software-only constraints.
